text: The soul would have no rainbow if the eyes had no tears.
author: Native American Proverb

text: The Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao. The name that can be named is not the eternal name.
author: Laozi

text: Water is the softest thing, yet it erodes mountains and stones. This is because it yields with ease. All things, one must change to be hard and stiff in order to resist death.
author: Laozi

text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
author: Laozi

text: The wise man does not lay up his own treasures. The more he gives to others, the more he has for his own.
author: Laozi

text: Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.
author: Laozi

text: To the mind that is still, the whole universe surrenders.
author: Laozi

text: Knowing others is wisdom. Knowing yourself is enlightenment.
author: Laozi

text: The greatest victories are those won without a fight. The sharpest edge is that which cuts no one.
author: Laozi

text: When you realize there is nothing lacking, the whole world belongs to you.
author: Laozi

text: The butterfly dreams it is a man. The man dreams he is a butterfly. Between the two, there must be a distinction — but which is the dream?
author: Zhuangzi

text: The universe is not something separate from you. You are the universe looking at itself.
author: Zhuangzi

text: Once you have looked beyond the boundaries of convention, you will never be confined by them again.
author: Zhuangzi

text: The fish trap exists because of the fish; once you have gotten the fish, you can forget the trap. The snare exists because of the rabbit; once you have gotten the rabbit, you can forget the snare.
author: Zhuangzi

text: To have attained the human form — just think how fortunate that is! To lose it again — just think how soon that comes! Yet a great master regards life as morning dew.
author: Zhuangzi

text: Ik Onkar — There is only One God. He is the Truth.
author: Guru Nanak

text: God is one; he who forgets God shall be destroyed. Nanak says, remember Him always.
author: Guru Nanak

text: There is no Muslim and no Hindu. There is only a human soul on a journey toward the light.
author: Guru Nanak

text: The world is not real, yet it is not unreal either. It is the stage upon which the soul plays its part.
author: Guru Nanak

text: He who has no faith in himself can never have faith in God.
author: Guru Nanak

text: Speak boldly and fearlessly, for the truth requires courage. The soldier of righteousness fears nothing but injustice.
author: Guru Gobind Singh

text: The Khalsa is the pure one. When the Khalsa is pure, God's glory is upheld.
author: Guru Gobind Singh

text: There is no place in this world that is free of God. He pervades all creation without exception.
author: Guru Gobind Singh

text: Naam Simran — remember God's name always. In that remembrance, you will find the peace that the world cannot give.
author: Guru Gobind Singh

text: The Guru is the light that dispels darkness. Seek the Guru, and you seek liberation.
author: Guru Arjan Dev

text: That which you call sin, the wise man calls opportunity. That which you call failure, the wise man calls learning.
author: Guru Tegh Bahadur

text: The Talmud teaches: He who saves a single soul, it is as if he has saved an entire world.
author: The Talmud

text: Rabbi Hillel taught: If I am not for myself, who will be for me? But if I am only for myself, what am I? And if not now, when?
author: Hillel the Elder

text: Do not judge your fellow man until you have reached his place.
author: Hillel the Elder

text: The Torah says: Love your neighbor as yourself. This is the greatest commandment in all the law.
author: Torah

text: Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One. Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
author: Torah

text: The measure of a man is not by what he accumulates, but by what he gives away. Generosity is the highest expression of faith.
author: The Talmud

text: Torah study is equivalent to all the commandments combined. It is the foundation upon which all of life rests.
author: The Talmud

text: A person who repents sincerely is greater than one who has never sinned at all.
author: The Talmud

text: Judaism teaches that God is not found only in heaven. He is found wherever you let Him in.
author: Maimonides

text: The purpose of the whole creation is to know God. Everything else is commentary.
author: Maimonides

text: The world was not created for your sake, but you were created for the sake of the world.
author: Elie Wiesel

text: Never shall I forget the first night, which made me forget so many things, which transformed my life into one long night.
author: Elie Wiesel

text: God's glory resides in questions, not in answers.
author: Rabbi Abraham Heschel

text: The Cherokee teach: Do not judge each day by the harvest you reap, but by the seeds that you plant.
author: Cherokee Proverb

text: The Lakota say: We are all related. Mitakuye Oyasin — all my relations.
author: Lakota Proverb

text: The earth does not belong to us; we belong to the earth.
author: Native American Proverb

text: The Navajo teach: Walk in beauty as it is here all around you. Above you walk in beauty, and through you.
author: Navajo Proverb

text: Listen to the wind, the tell, the rain falling. Listen to yourself.
author: Apache Proverb

text: The Ojibwe say: Look behind you and see all in peace, and ahead you see all in victory.
author: Ojibwe Proverb

text: When you were born, you cried and the world rejoiced. Live your life so that when you die, the world cries and you rejoice.
author: Native American Proverb

text: The Crow nation says: Do not judge another person until you have walked a long distance in their moccasins.
author: Crow Proverb

text: The Sioux teach: The heart has always been the place closest to the spirit. Listen to yours.
author: Sioux Proverb

text: It takes a village to raise a child.
author: African Proverb

text: A child who is not embraced by the village will be reclaimed by it to burn it down.
author: African Proverb

text: No one is as wise as the person who has learned from everyone.
author: African Proverb

text: When the music changes, so does the dance.
author: African Proverb

text: The river does not ask for permission to flow. It simply moves in the direction of its nature.
author: African Proverb

text: Until the lions have their own historians, the history of the hunt will always favor the hunter.
author: African Proverb

text: A man who is not brave enough to take a risk, anything he does will be mediocre.
author: African Proverb

text: The elders are the library of the community. When an elder dies, a library is burned.
author: African Proverb

text: If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together.
author: African Proverb

text: The rain does not fall on one roof alone. Every soul is touched by grace.
author: African Proverb

text: Ubuntu: I am because we are. A person is a person through other persons.
author: African Proverb

text: The Zulu say: Even the mightiest tree bends in the storm. Strength is not in standing rigid; it is in bending without breaking.
author: Zulu Proverb

text: The land is sacred. Those who walked it before us, and those who walk it after us — they are all one with the earth.
author: Australian Aboriginal Wisdom

text: The Dreaming is not a time in the past. It is happening now, in every breath, in every stone, in every creature.
author: Australian Aboriginal Wisdom

text: We did not inherit the land from our ancestors; we borrowed it from our children.
author: Australian Aboriginal Wisdom

text: The stars are the ancestors watching over us. Every night, they return to remind us where we came from.
author: Australian Aboriginal Wisdom

text: Country holds the soul. When you are separated from it, part of your spirit goes quiet.
author: Australian Aboriginal Wisdom

text: Kia ora — life is a gift. Receive it with open hands and a grateful heart.
author: Maori Proverb

text: He aha te mea nui o te ao? He tangata, he tangata, he tangata. What is the greatest thing in the world? It is the people, the people, the people.
author: Maori Proverb

text: The whakapapa — the genealogy of all living things — connects us to every creature and to the gods themselves.
author: Maori Proverb

text: The sacred fire has burned since the beginning. It asks nothing of you but that you tend it with reverence.
author: Indigenous Wisdom

text: Ask not what the world owes you. Ask what you owe the world. That is the beginning of wisdom.
author: Indigenous Wisdom

text: Good thoughts, good words, good deeds. These three are the pillars upon which all truth stands.
author: Zarathustra

text: The battle is not between good and evil on the outside. It is within. Purify your own mind, and you purify the world.
author: Zarathustra

text: Light is the symbol of truth and righteousness. Walk ever toward it, never away.
author: Zarathustra

text: Ahura Mazda created the world in perfection. It is man's task to restore it when it has been made imperfect.
author: Zarathustra

text: Righteousness is the foundation of all things. Without it, even the mightiest kingdom crumbles to dust.
author: Zarathustra

text: The unity of God is the first truth. All other truths flow from this single, infinite source.
author: Bahá'u'lláh

text: The religions of the world are not enemies of one another. They are rivers flowing into the same ocean of truth.
author: Bahá'u'lláh

text: Treat thy neighbor even as thyself. Let no man's ignorance dim the light of thy love.
author: Bahá'u'lláh

text: The purpose of life is to unite the world in one common faith, one shared justice, and one universal peace.
author: Abdul-Baha

text: The light of the knowledge of God shall pervade the world; all nations shall become as one.
author: Abdul-Baha

text: Ahimsa — non-violence — is the highest virtue. One who practices it truly has conquered the self.
author: Lord Mahavira

text: All souls in the universe have the same divine nature. The difference is only in the layers of karma that cover them.
author: Lord Mahavira

text: Every soul is a king. Know yourself, and you know your kingdom.
author: Lord Mahavira

text: Faith without practice is like a seed without soil. It has the potential for great things, but without nourishment, it cannot grow.
author: Lord Mahavira

text: The soul, freed from all attachment, shines with an infinite radiance. This is liberation.
author: Lord Mahavira

text: Your children need your presence more than your possessions.
author: Khalil Gibran

text: On giving: There are those who give with joy, and that joy is their reward and their plenty.
author: Khalil Gibran

text: Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding.
author: Khalil Gibran

text: Out of suffering have emerged the greatest souls. The most mournful of creatures are the most blessed.
author: Khalil Gibran

text: The soul unfolds itself, not in one but in many steps. Each step is a new dawn.
author: Rumi

text: The heart knows truths that the mind can never reach. Trust the heart.
author: Rumi

text: The universe is not outside of you. Look inside yourself; everything that you want, you already are.
author: Deepak Chopra

text: The secret of attraction is to love yourself. Attractive people judge neither themselves nor others.
author: Deepak Chopra

text: All faiths are roads. All religions soar to the same spirit, then stumble the moment they turn concrete into the divine.
author: Spiritual Proverb

text: The divine does not live in temples or mosques. The divine lives in the space between two hearts that understand each other.
author: Spiritual Proverb

text: Every tradition names the sacred differently. Every tradition points toward the same light.
author: Spiritual Proverb

text: The universe conspires to bring the seeker to what is sought. Trust the journey.
author: Spiritual Proverb

text: Compassion is the language all religions speak. It is the thread that binds all of humanity together.
author: Spiritual Proverb

text: The greatest prayer is not the one spoken with words. It is the one lived with every breath.
author: Spiritual Proverb

text: In the silence between the stars, the sacred whispers. Listen, and you will hear it speak your name.
author: Spiritual Proverb
